result.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models
result.summary: If we optimize an image until a classifier is confident it shows a cat, we may get an adversarial example, not a cat. Planning with a latent world model is a similar search for actions whose predicted future is closest to the goal. Is the result a plan, or an adversarial example of the world model? We show that it can be either. On the released DINO-WM and LeWM, more iterations of the cross-entropy method (CEM) lower the predicted cost but lose up to half of the problems CEM had already solved. The model's own predictions do not reveal these failures. We propose a simple test that executes the plan after every iteration and counts the problems a planner solves and then loses. Unlike an image, a plan comes with its actions, which our round-trip check reads back from the predicted states with a small network, penalizing mismatches. The check reads back the sum of each block of five actions, the part that two consecutive predicted states determine. Without retraining the world model and at only 0.2% to 3.1% more planning time, it improves the widely used planners CEM and MPPI on three released world models, and gains more where planners lose more problems. Without replanning, success rises from 0.39 to 0.76 on Wall with DINO-WM and from 0.56 to 0.94 for MPPI on JEPA-WM. With replanning (MPC), it rises from 0.70 to 0.81 on Cube with LeWM.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验 latent world model 规划结果究竟是「计划」还是模型的对抗样本，发现 CEM 迭代越多预测代价越低、却丢掉已解问题，且模型自身预测不暴露这些失败；为此提出 round-trip check，用小网络从预测状态反解动作块之和并惩罚不一致，在不重训模型、仅增 0.2%–3.1% 规划时间下改进 CEM 与 MPPI。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测代价下降但真实成功下降、模型内部信号无法自证」的诊断与反解一致性校验，可能为 LVR 的停止决策、latent 内容是否被真正使用及推理结果验证提供可核查线索。
